title: OPT 370 Special Ophthalmic Lenses candidate bank

objectives.statement: Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for lenticular and aspheric lenses.
Apply and analyse lenticular and aspheric lenses in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.
Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for aniseikonia and iseikonic lenses.
Apply and analyse aniseikonia and iseikonic lenses in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.
Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for spectacle magnification.
Apply and analyse spectacle magnification in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.
Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for safety lenses, filters and coatings.
Apply and analyse safety lenses, filters and coatings in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.
Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for fresnel prism fitting.
Apply and analyse fresnel prism fitting in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.
Explain the core terminology, relationships and course-source principles for bicentric grinding and slab-off.
Apply and analyse bicentric grinding and slab-off in calculations, diagrams, fitting decisions or error analysis.

questions.stem: Using the lecture formulas, analyse a +4.00 D lens with front curve +10.00 D, centre thickness 6 mm, index 1.50 and vertex distance 15 mm. Calculate shape factor, power factor, total spectacle magnification and percentage magnification, then explain how two design variables could reduce magnification.
questions.explanation: S = [1-(0.006/1.50)(10)]^-1 = 1.042. P = [1-(0.015)(4)]^-1 = 1.0638. SM = 1.1085, so magnification is 10.85%. Magnification could be reduced by moving the plus lens closer to the eye and/or using a flatter, thinner, higher-index form, subject to optical and manufacturing limits.
